"ELDORIA: THE LOST REALMS

COMPLETE REBUILD — FROM ZERO

IMPORTANT: DISCARD THE PREVIOUS GAME BUILD AND RECREATE THE ENTIRE PROJECT FROM SCRATCH.

Do not reuse the previous character model, environment, map layout, visual template, placeholder assets, UI layout, or existing gameplay implementation.

This is a complete rebuild, not an update.

1. GAME IDENTITY

- Title: ELDORIA: THE LOST REALMS
- Genre: 3D Open-World Medieval Fantasy RPG
- Perspective: Third-person
- Mode: Single-player
- Platform: Android mobile and PC
- World: Seamless explorable fantasy environment
- Visual direction: High-quality 3D fantasy adventure, detailed materials, natural lighting, atmospheric environments.

2. COMPLETELY NEW 3D CHARACTER

Create an entirely new player character.

Requirements:

- Detailed humanoid 3D model.
- Proper body proportions and anatomy.
- Separate head, torso, arms, hands, legs and equipment.
- Detailed clothing, armor and materials.
- Natural walking, running, jumping and combat animations.
- Smooth character movement and turning.
- Proper collision and physics.

Do not use the old character model or primitive capsule-shaped placeholder characters.

3. NEW OPEN WORLD

Create an original, fully explorable medieval fantasy world.

Environment:

- Large forests with varied tree species.
- Detailed grass, plants and vegetation.
- Mountains, hills and valleys.
- Rivers, lakes and waterfalls.
- Medieval villages and castles.
- Stone bridges, roads and ruins.
- Caves and hidden exploration areas.
- Detailed terrain with elevation changes.

The environment must not look like a collection of simple geometric primitives.

4. GRAPHICS AND RENDERING

Implement the best visual quality supported by the game engine.

Prioritize:

- High-quality PBR materials.
- Detailed textures.
- Dynamic sunlight.
- Real-time shadows.
- Ambient occlusion.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Realistic water reflections.
- Dynamic sky and clouds.
- Day and night cycle.
- Natural environmental lighting.
- Improved terrain and vegetation rendering.

Do not simulate high-quality graphics using only flat colors and simple geometric shapes.

5. REAL PHYSICS SYSTEM

Physics must be implemented as actual interactive gameplay systems, not merely visual effects.

Requirements:

- Gravity.
- Collision detection.
- Rigid-body physics where supported.
- Mass and object weight.
- Friction and bouncing.
- Object interaction.
- Character-ground collision.
- Proper jumping and falling.
- Water interaction.
- Environmental collision.
- Physics-based object movement.

Objects should respond appropriately when the player interacts with them.

Trees, rocks, buildings and other static environmental objects must have appropriate collision boundaries.

6. WATER AND ENVIRONMENTAL SIMULATION

Water:

- Animated water surfaces.
- Waves and ripples.
- Reflections.
- Shoreline interaction.
- Visual response to nearby moving objects where supported.

Vegetation:

- Wind animation.
- Moving leaves and grass.
- Natural environmental movement.

Weather:

- Rain.
- Fog.
- Wind.
- Cloud movement.
- Environmental lighting changes.

7. MOBILE CONTROLS

Mobile controls are mandatory.

Portrait and landscape layouts must both work.

Left side:

- Virtual joystick.
- UP = move forward.
- DOWN = move backward.
- LEFT = move left.
- RIGHT = move right.

Right side:

- Camera control.
- Jump.
- Attack.
- Guard.
- Dodge.
- Interaction.

The joystick must remain fixed on the LEFT side of the screen.

Movement must be camera-relative and responsive.

IMPORTANT:

- Detect touch devices correctly.
- Never display PC keyboard instructions as the only controls on mobile.
- Never hide the virtual joystick in landscape mode.
- Automatically adjust HUD positions to screen dimensions.
- Prevent buttons from overlapping.
- Support different Android screen aspect ratios.

8. PC CONTROLS

PC controls:

- WASD: movement.
- Mouse: camera.
- Space: jump.
- Shift: dodge.
- E: interaction.
- Mouse buttons: combat.

Mobile and PC input systems must work independently.

9. GAMEPLAY SYSTEMS

Implement:

- Exploration.
- Main quests.
- Side quests.
- NPC dialogue.
- Enemy AI.
- Combat.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Character progression.
- Health and stamina.
- Collectible resources.
- Save and load.

NPCs should have functional interactions rather than being decorative objects.

10. CAMERA AND ANIMATION

Implement a proper third-person camera:

- Smooth camera rotation.
- Adjustable camera distance.
- Collision avoidance.
- Smooth camera follow.
- No camera clipping through terrain or buildings.

Character animations must transition smoothly between movement states.

11. PERFORMANCE

Optimize for Android devices, including mid-range hardware.

Requirements:

- Adaptive graphics quality.
- Level of detail (LOD).
- Efficient shadows.
- Optimized textures.
- Efficient object rendering.
- Controlled draw calls.
- Stable frame rate.
- No unnecessary background processing.

Do not sacrifice basic gameplay functionality for visual effects.

12. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Build in this order:

1. Create a completely new project and remove old implementation.
2. Build the new character and animation system.
3. Build the new 3D world and terrain.
4. Implement physics and collision.
5. Implement water and environmental simulation.
6. Implement mobile and PC controls.
7. Implement camera and gameplay.
8. Add NPCs, enemies and quests.
9. Optimize performance.
10. Test the complete game.

13. FINAL QUALITY REQUIREMENTS

The result must be visibly different from the previous ELDORIA build.

Do not simply add more trees, houses or NPCs to the old world.

Do not claim that physics, reflections, animations or interactions are implemented unless they actually work.

If a feature is unsupported by the engine, explain the limitation instead of faking the feature.

Build a playable, functional 3D fantasy RPG with a completely new visual identity.

FINAL INSTRUCTION: REBUILD EVERYTHING FROM ZERO. DO NOT PRESERVE THE OLD GAME'S VISUAL TEMPLATE OR IMPLEMENTATION.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

There’s no existing game source to preserve or rebuild on top of—the repository currently contains only project metadata and launcher scripts. I’m creating a fresh browser-based 3D RPG instead, with procedural terrain and scenery, an articulated player, working combat/exploration systems, and touch-first controls that also support PC input.

*** Add File: README.md
+# ELDORIA: THE LOST REALMS
+
+A fresh, browser-playable third-person fantasy RPG prototype. Serve this directory over HTTP (for example, `python3 -m http.server 8000`) and open `http://localhost:8000`. The game loads Three.js from jsDelivr, so an internet connection is required.
+
+## Controls
+
+- **PC:** WASD/arrows move; drag the mouse to orbit; left click attacks; right mouse button or Q guards; Space jumps; Shift dodges; E interacts; Esc opens the journal.
+- **Touch:** fixed left-side joystick moves; drag the right side to look; on-screen buttons jump, strike, guard, dodge and interact. Portrait and landscape layouts are supported.
+
+Explore the vale, activate the glowing waystone, fight roaming sentinels, gather drops and save/load progress from the journal.
+
+## Scope and limitations
+
+This is a playable prototype built from procedural Three.js geometry and locally implemented gameplay. The character uses a custom articulated mesh with procedural movement poses, not motion-captured animation. Terrain collisions, gravity, jumping, enemy pursuit/knockback and movement are implemented in game logic; there is no general rigid-body physics engine, physical mass/friction simulation, or water-body interaction. Water is a translucent animated-looking surface with ripples, not a reflection-rendered fluid simulation. Lighting, fog, wind-swaying vegetation and a simple daylight shift are present; there are no detailed imported PBR texture assets, dynamic clouds, rain system, full quest/dialogue framework, or native Android package. Mobile play is through the responsive browser interface.
*** End Patch

content.text:
Built a fresh playable Three.js RPG prototype with a new articulated character, procedural fantasy valley, mobile/PC controls, combat, roaming enemies, a waystone quest, inventory, and local save/load.

Run it with `python3 -m http.server 8000`, then open `http://localhost:8000`. Three.js loads from a CDN, so internet access is required. `node --check game.js` passes.

This is a prototype, not a production-scale RPG: it uses procedural geometry and game-logic collisions, not scanned assets, a rigid-body physics engine, motion-captured animations, or realistic water reflections. Other limitations and controls are documented in `README.md`.
